title: Token Stewardship Panel — Compact UX & Chart Specs
creator: Amaya Chen
description: Design a compact 'Token Stewardship' panel for the Redwood Console that surfaces per-model and per-route token economics and performance. Panel must live as a collapsible card on model and route pages and be reusable in aggregated views. Visuals: token flow sparkline, per-token latency violin, cost waterfall by stage (prompt/stream/generation), KV cache hit donut, and throughput heatline. Primary goal: enable engineers and product owners to quickly diagnose token-related regressions and cost anomalies, and to link to rollouts and prompt sets.
acceptance_criteria: Compact card renders correctly at 280-420px widths with responsive microcharts
Charts update in <500ms in the console when receiving telemetry snapshots
Each mini-chart has explainer tooltip and 'Open in Metrics Explorer' link
Cost waterfall shows breakdown by token stage and highlights >10% regressions
Design sign-off from Eng (runtime) and PM; accessibility contrast >= 4.5:1 for critical data
Prototype handoff includes Figma frames, token palette tokens, and CSS variables

ux_notes: Microchart choices: sparkline for token trend, violin for latency distribution to show skew, waterfall for cost decomposition, donut for cache hit ratio, and heatline for throughput/time-of-day spikes
Interaction: hover reveals 3-line summary (median latency, 95p latency, tokens/min) plus 'Open in Explore' and 'Pin to Briefing' actions
Density tradeoff: at narrow widths icons and labels collapse to tooltips; use micro-annotations rather than full legends
Color palette: primary token color = #3B82F6, cost delta = diverging red/green with 20% desaturation, cache hit = teal; ensure colorblind-safe palette
Data keys mapped: tokens_total, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, token_cost_usd, latency_p50, latency_p95, cache_hit_rate
design_decisions: Use waterfall instead of stacked bars to make stage-level cost deltas obvious during rollouts
Introduce violin plot for latency because mean/median alone hide heavy tails caused by long-generation tails
Keep single-line title + small sublabel to preserve card compactness
Add persistent 'Compare with baseline' toggle linked to selected rollout or past 24h median
open_questions: Should we show absolute cost in cents or normalized cost-per-1k-tokens by default? PM prefers cents for clarity.
How to label 'prompt' vs 'input' tokens consistently across console and billing?
Do we need a lightweight fallback for low telemetry windows (zero-fill vs hide chart)?
handoff_checklist: Figma frames exported with tokens and annotations
Chart spec table with axis units, sampling cadence, allowed null behavior
CSS variable map and token colors
Engineers assigned: Jared Moss (runtime), Leila Park (frontend)
